devices.name: Metonymy
devices.definition: Naming something by a word closely associated with it — cause for effect, container for contents, author for writings.

occurrences.note: " Sheba fell upon them ": i.e., the Sabeans, as in A.V
"Thou shalt be hid from the scourge (i.e., power) of the tongue."
"At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh ": i.e., thou shalt be secure against them
"Oh that I might have my request; and that God would grant me my expectation ": i.e., the object of my prayer and desire
" Till he fill thy mouth with laughing (i.e., rejoicing), and thy lips with shouting for joy."
" The secrets of wisdom are double to that which is ": i.e., far beyond, or much more
"And above the noonday shall be thy time ": i.e., thy prosperity shall be brighter and clearer than noon
"Their belly prepareth deceit": i.e., their thoughts and desires
To put hands on the head is put for grief
"They that come after him shall be astonied at his day ": i.e., at his fate
"And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand": i.e., I have made the outward sign of worship or homage
" I said, Days (i.e., men of days, or men of full age) should speak, and multitude of years (i.e., aged men) should teach wisdom."

devices.name: Ellipsis
devices.definition: A word or words deliberately left out, to be supplied by the reader — compression and force.

occurrences.note: " As the stream of brooks they pass away."
"Who hath divided a watercourse," and

devices.name: Anthropopatheia
devices.definition: Ascribing to God human feelings, parts, or actions, by way of condescension to us.

occurrences.note: " By the breath of his nostrils are they consumed." The A.V. margin says " That is, by his anger,"
" Thine hands have made me and fashioned me."
" The hand of Jehovah hath wrought this."
" In whose hand is the life of every living thing."
"The hand of God (Eloah) hath touched me."
" His eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings."
" Hast thou an arm like God ? "

devices.name: Idiom
devices.definition: A peculiar usage of the Hebrew or Greek that does not carry its literal force — an idiom to be rendered by its sense, not word for word.

occurrences.note: meant to attempt, to try. " Beeves "
meant to conclude a bargain by shaking hands. "Trow"

devices.name: Paroemia (proverb)
devices.definition: A proverb — a wayside-saying in common use, cited or coined.

occurrences.note: says: " Man is born unto trouble,"
" Doth the wild ass bray when he is at grass ? or loweth the ox over his fodder ? "
" The waters wear the stones."
"The price of wisdom is above rubies."
passed into a common proverb

devices.name: Personification
devices.definition: Giving human traits, action, or speech to something impersonal or abstract.

occurrences.note: " Ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee: and the fowls of the air, they shall tell thee."
" Destruction and death say. We have heard of the fame thereof with our ears."
"When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God (i.e., the angels) shouted for joy." The stars are also called on to praise God

devices.name: Synecdoche
devices.definition: Substituting a part for the whole, or the whole for a part (“all the world”; “flesh and blood”).

occurrences.note: " Which removeth mountains, and they know not." This is only one kind of things which are possible with God, though impossible with men
"Many shall intreat thy face": i.e., as in A.V., " will make suit unto thee."
"All the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come ": i.e., till I die: dying being one of many changes experienced by man
Job is named, but the others are included

devices.name: Heterosis
devices.definition: Exchange of one grammatical form for another — of tense, number, person, degree, or mood (e.g. a future used for a command).

devices.name: Hyperbole
devices.definition: Deliberate exaggeration, not meant literally, that drives a point home vividly.

occurrences.note: Job's grief heavier than the sand
"The rock poured me out rivers of oil": i.e., I had abundance of all good things. So chap
Leviathan's sneezings causing light to shine

devices.name: Rhetorical question
devices.definition: A question asked for effect, not for an answer — to affirm, deny, or provoke thought.

devices.name: Enigma
devices.definition: A dark saying — a truth wrapped in obscure or riddling terms.

devices.name: Euphemism
devices.definition: A softened or decent expression put for one that is harsh or delicate (“fallen asleep”).

occurrences.note: " The first-born of death shall devour his strength": i.e., the cruellest and most calamitous death shall destroy him
Death is called "the king of terrors": i.e., the terrible king who claims so many subjects

devices.name: Irony
devices.definition: Saying the opposite of what is meant, so the real sense is felt through the contrast.

occurrences.note: " Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth ? " Verse 5. " Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest ? or who hath stretched the line upon it ? " So throughout this chapter

devices.name: Paronomasia (wordplay)
devices.definition: A play on words that sound alike but differ in sense — pun, rhyme, near-repetition.

devices.name: Periphrasis
devices.definition: Circumlocution: a description put in place of the plain name of a thing.

devices.name: Catachresis
devices.definition: One word used for another only remotely related — a deliberately incongruous transfer.

occurrences.note: " Now a word was brought by stealth to me." This is a most unusual way of describing an angelic communication

devices.name: Gnome (quotation)
devices.definition: A quotation or proverbial maxim woven in — a pithy saying cited for authority or point.

devices.name: Hendiadys
devices.definition: One idea expressed by two words joined with “and,” the second really qualifying the first.

occurrences.note: " Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death ": i.e., the land of darkness, yes — and the darkness of death's shadow too

devices.name: Epanadiplosis
devices.definition: A clause encircled — beginning and ending with the same word.

devices.name: Hypallage
devices.definition: Interchange: a word logically belonging to one term is grammatically attached to another.

devices.name: Oxymoron / paradox
devices.definition: A pointed pairing of apparently contradictory terms that expresses a deeper truth.

devices.name: Pleonasm
devices.definition: A deliberate redundancy — more words than strictly needed — to underline or solemnise.

devices.name: Polysyndeton
devices.definition: Conjunctions (“and … and …”) piled up to slow the pace and weight every item.
